The not-equal sign has two even horizontal strokes and a mechanically heavy diagonal. It does not share the fine flowing texture of the inserted membership signs. I treat the relation as typed; the letter is discussed separately.

differences.H: \ell; note: Le $\ell$ de la machine, partout, est un caractère en forme de $\chi$
differences.ink: The glyph has a left upper hook, diagonal rising to the right, a triangular lower crossing, and a horizontal foot. Those peculiar forms recur mechanically in the prose and the subscript. Its shape is chi-like; ell is retained first but not imposed solely by the prime-number context.
differences.math_consequence: Identifies the prime-number parameter; the role is clear even though its glyph family is not.

The distinctive diagonal, upper hook, and pointed lower foot repeat the first prime glyph and the coefficient subscript. This is evidence for a typewriter glyph rather than a separate handwritten insertion at each place.
There is a single typed Z with its ordinary diagonal and serifs; a separate horizontal rule lies below it. Heavy impression is not a bold or double-struck alphabet.
The subscript repeats the exact angular prime glyph including its hook and foot, at a shifted baseline. I treat it as typed; the separate underlining belongs to Z.
An open curved epsilon-like stroke plus short horizontal bar is pen-written between typed x and H.
The capital N remains recognizable above H. Lower, overlaid small humps are closest to m. The overlap warrants keeping the live m marked uncertain.
differences.math_consequence: Live degree is read m, with original N retained as a cancelled layer.

The enlargement shows one E stem, the ordinary three arms, and serifs. There is heavy/uneven impression, but no convincing separate doubled stem establishing a blackboard alphabet.

The glyph has a Z-height upper bar and a lower bar, with a short extra interior stroke. This is consistent with a retraced or superposed Z/z, but does not securely establish a separate double-struck diagonal. Ordinary Z is the closest live candidate; case remains open here.

notes: The page opens a section entitled Le théorème de Griffiths par voie algébrique. It assumes a proper smooth morphism f:Y→S with S regular and connected, residue characteristics different from the prime parameter, and a twisted constant adic coefficient sheaf F.

Primitive means that the image in H^0(S,R^m f_*(F)) vanishes, with an asserted equivalent vanishing on a geometric fibre. The word primitive is explicitly underlined. This is the page’s definition; no Lefschetz-style replacement is introduced.

The page assigns a Leray class u(x) in E_2^{1,m-1}=H^1(S,R^{m-1}f_*(F_Y)). Several degree and direct-image components have been corrected; clear live indices are distinguished from uncertain old layers.

A correspondence class in H^N(Y x_S Y\prime,G), together with F\prime tensor G→F(d\prime), is said to act from H^{m\prime}(Y\prime,F\prime) to H^m(Y,F). The visible live degree relation is m=m\prime+N-2d\prime.
The author states preservation of primitive classes and u(Z(x\prime))=Z(u(x\prime)); the explanatory sentence continues beyond this page. No continuation is supplied or inferred.

The author has no explicit verbal reservation on this page. NB introduces explanations of d\prime, the relative dimension, and the Tate twist. The assertions include ou ce qui revient au même and évidemment; these are transcribed without endorsing their generality.

Mathematical parsing prompted special attention to the degree correction and the parentheses of the primitive-image formula. Ink, not the expected trace degree, determines the reading 2d\prime. The crossed coefficient block includes both cancelled closing brackets.

No OCR, web search, published transcription, other page image, other reader output, or external literature was used. The notation input contained only its header, so no earlier alphabet convention was imposed.

check_events.outcome: Assuming a convergent first-quadrant cohomological Leray spectral sequence with d_r of bidegree (r,1-r), a primitive class lies in F^1H^m. Its quotient in gr_F^1 is E_infinity^{1,m-1}. For r≥2 no incoming differential has nonnegative first index, so E_infinity^{1,m-1} embeds into E_2^{1,m-1} through the successive kernels. This checks the formal possibility of the displayed u(x), without verifying convergence, adic formalism, or the claimed specialization equivalence.

Assuming the correspondence action consists of pullback from Y\prime, cup product with a degree-N class, and trace along a projection of relative dimension d\prime lowering degree by 2d\prime, the degree is m\prime+N-2d\prime. Assuming the trace removes the d\prime Tate twist, F\prime tensor G→F(d\prime) yields coefficients F. This matches the visible corrected formula; it does not establish existence or all hypotheses of the action.
